senses.gloss: (b. h.) [to cut, point,] to be sharp, pointed.
to sharpen, whet, point. Y. Bets. V, 63ᵇ top לחַדֵּד ראשו וכ׳ they differ as to pointing the top of the spit (on the Holy Day)—Trnsf. to whet the mind, to try somebody’s acumen, to puzzle.
units: <cite ref="Taanit 7a:8">Taan. 7ᵃ</cite> (ref. to <cite ref="Proverbs 27:17">Prov. XXVII, 17</cite>) <he>אף … מְחַדְּדִין וכ׳</he> so do two scholars whet each other’s mind &c.
Naz. 59ᵇ, a. e. לא אמר … לחַדֵּד בה וכ׳ R. J. said it only in order to encourage the students in raising points; a. e.—Part. pass. מְחוּדָּד sharpened, well discussed, clear and ready.

<cite ref="Kiddushin 30a:15">Kidd. 30ᵃ</cite> (ref. to <he>ושננתם</he>, <cite ref="Deuteronomy 6:7">Deut. VI, 7</cite>) <he>שיהו ד״ת מְחוּדָּדִים בפיך</he> that the words of the Law be ever ready in thy mouth (<cite ref="Sifrei Devarim 34:1">Sifré Deut. 34</cite> <he>מְסוּדָּרִים</he>), v. <cite ref="C00998"><he>גִּמְגֵּם</he></cite>.

<cite ref="Bereishit Rabbah 69:2">Gen. R. s. 69</cite> <he>אין סכין מִתְחַדֶּדֶת וכ׳</he> a knife is whetted on the broad side of another, <he>כך אין ת״ח מִתְחַדֵּד וכ׳</he> so is a student’s mind whetted by a fellow-student, v. supra.
